memory_update.text: AMZN, WMT, CART, TGT, and DASH are the highest-priority direct public candidates for ecommerce marketplace, retail media, first-party shopper data, and attribution exposure in this pass.

The strongest node relation appears where a company controls discovery, checkout, transaction data, and ad inventory simultaneously; this creates a potential monetization flywheel through seller services, sponsored placement, and closed-loop measurement.

Potential follow-up names excluded due to the 5-candidate limit include EBAY, ETSY, KR, COST, BBY, UBER, PINS, TTD, ROKU, and ad-tech or measurement vendors tied to commerce media; these should be screened in a later adjacent-node or enabler pass.

Need a future evidence pass to normalize retail media exposure by revenue share, gross margin contribution, disclosed ad revenue, traffic quality, marketplace GMV, seller dependence, and whether ad spend is incremental or a reallocation from trade promotion budgets.
Add AMZN, WMT, CART, CRTO, and RAMP to the ecommerce_retail_media_data watchlist as direct or second-order exposure to retail-media data and attribution chokepoints.

The key bottleneck is not ecommerce traffic alone; it is the combination of first-party transaction data, ad inventory, search/ranking control, checkout/fulfillment linkage, and closed-loop attribution.

Marketplace owners AMZN, WMT, and CART have stronger direct chokepoint control than ad-tech suppliers because they control purchase intent and transaction data; CRTO and RAMP are infrastructure/enabler candidates and require more evidence on revenue durability and customer concentration.

Potential additional candidates for later passes include TTD for retail-data programmatic activation, ROKU for CTV commerce-media inventory and Walmart/Instacart/Kroger partnerships, DV for ad verification, and consumer brands with heavy marketplace advertising exposure.
For ecommerce_retail_media_data, add CART, EBAY, UBER, EXPE, and CRTO as direct or adjacent US-listed candidates; CRTO should carry a below-1B exception flag.
The node is best mapped as a monetization layer on top of consumer intent: owned transaction data, sponsored ranking, seller/brand ad spend, checkout attribution, and marketplace/retailer APIs.

Obvious leaders AMZN and WMT were not included in the 5-name candidate cap for this pass because the search focus favored less obvious second-order beneficiaries; they remain benchmark comparables for ad scale, closed-loop data, and margin contribution.

Next pass should test additional nodes: SHOP as merchant operating system/Shop Campaigns, TTD as open-web retail-media demand-side infrastructure, ROKU/VZIO/WMT CTV-commerce data, and consumer brands highly exposed to marketplace ad taxes.
